title: Core ideas in physics
description: The laws behind motion, energy, light and matter, with the numbers worth knowing.

ideas.title: Newton's laws of motion
ideas.summary: An object keeps its velocity unless a net force acts on it, and the force needed is mass times acceleration.

items.q: What does Newton's first law of motion say?
items.a: An object stays at rest or moves at constant velocity unless a net force acts on it

items.q: What equation states Newton's second law of motion?
items.a: F = ma: net force equals mass times acceleration

items.q: What does Newton's third law of motion say?
items.a: Every force has an equal and opposite partner: if A pushes on B, B pushes back on A just as hard

items.q: In physics, what is the product of an object's mass and its velocity called?
items.a: Momentum

ideas.title: Gravity
ideas.summary: Every mass attracts every other mass, with a force that weakens as the square of the distance between them.

items.q: How does Newtonian gravitational force between two point masses change if their separation doubles?
items.a: It falls to one quarter, because gravity follows an inverse square law

items.q: What is the acceleration of a freely falling object near Earth's surface?
items.a: About 9.8 m/s^2

items.q: In physics, what is the difference between mass and weight?
items.a: Mass is the amount of matter in an object; weight is the force of gravity on it

items.q: In which book, published in 1687, did Isaac Newton set out his laws of motion and of universal gravitation?
items.a: The Principia (Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica)

ideas.title: Conservation of energy
ideas.summary: Energy is never created or destroyed, only moved from place to place or changed from one form to another.

items.q: What does the law of conservation of energy say?
items.a: Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred or changed from one form to another

items.q: What is the formula for the kinetic energy of a mass m moving at speed v?
items.a: KE = 1/2 m v^2

items.q: What is the SI unit of energy?
items.a: The joule (J)

items.q: What is the SI unit of power, equal to one joule per second?
items.a: The watt (W)

ideas.title: Heat and entropy
ideas.summary: Heat flows by itself from hot to cold, and the entropy of an isolated system never decreases.

items.q: What does the second law of thermodynamics say about the entropy of an isolated system?
items.a: It never decreases: it rises or, at best, stays the same

items.q: What is absolute zero in degrees Celsius?
items.a: -273.15 °C, which is 0 kelvin

items.q: For a classical ideal gas, what particle-motion quantity is proportional to its absolute temperature?
items.a: The average translational kinetic energy per particle

items.q: Left to itself, in which direction does heat flow between two bodies in contact?
items.a: From the hotter body to the colder one

ideas.title: Electromagnetism and light
ideas.summary: Electricity and magnetism are two sides of one force, and light is a wave in the electromagnetic field.

items.q: What is the speed of light in a vacuum?
items.a: About 3 x 10^8 m/s (exactly 299,792,458 m/s)

items.q: Which physicist united electricity, magnetism and light in one set of equations in the 1860s?
items.a: James Clerk Maxwell

items.q: For any wave, how are speed, frequency and wavelength related?
items.a: Speed = frequency x wavelength

items.q: What is the rule for the force between electric charges of the same sign and of opposite sign?
items.a: Like charges repel; opposite charges attract

ideas.title: Relativity and the quantum
ideas.summary: At very high speeds and very small scales, Newton's picture gives way to relativity and quantum mechanics.

items.q: What does Einstein's equation E = mc^2 say?
items.a: Mass and energy are equivalent: energy equals mass times the speed of light squared

items.q: How does Einstein's general theory of relativity, published in 1915, describe gravity?
items.a: As the curving of spacetime by mass and energy

items.q: In physics, what is a photon?
items.a: A quantum of light: a single packet of electromagnetic energy

items.q: What does Heisenberg's uncertainty principle say about a particle's position and momentum?
items.a: Both cannot be known precisely at the same time
